prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian region airspace near capacity; airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. System: Regional Flow Platform (alias Cedarbell), ATFM/A-CDM coordination layer; doesn't replace ATC/airport/airline/handling ops. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (alias Marlinstone), Capacity Assessment Module (CAM), Slot Allocation Engine, Airport CDM Portal, Digital Briefing Room, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, Contingency Operations Console, Weather Ingest Gateway (WIG, alias Orchard), Flight Data Exchange, Surface Surveillance Adapter, Airline Interface Adapter, Alert Distribution Hub, Performance Analytics Warehouse, Audit Event Ledger, Identity Access Service, Business Rules Registry (BRR), Time Synchronization Service, Collaborative Decision Log, North/South Runway Meter, East/West Apron Sensor, Sector Load Monitor, Gate Conflict Detector, Common Situation Display. External (authenticated, audited): airline reservation, crew, baggage, commercial, national surveillance, avionics. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (RFM, alias Copperfin), Airline Operations Coordinator, Network Operations Liaison, Aircraft Operator Representative, Slot Coordinator, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Airport Duty Manager, Ground Handling Dispatcher, Handling Resource Planner, Deicing Coordinator, Meteorology Briefing Officer, Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator, Data Governance Steward, System Support Engineer. Items: Flight Intent Message (FIM), Airport Capacity Plan, Target Off Block Time, Calculated Takeoff Time, Airport Acceptance Rate (AAR), Tactical Regulation Proposal, Ground Delay Program status, Storm Cell Snapshot, Runway Inspection Note, Decision Log entries, Post Operations Report. Modes: Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, Slot Compliance State. Reqs: no binding CTTs in baseline; post-approval changes only via controlled functions; Metering Service/Arrival Console used only under accountable flow roles, outputs visible on Common Situation Display; escalate to Emergency Response Coordinator on safety/security/emergency events affecting acceptance, surface or airspace; Steward verifies decisions/acknowledgements/exceptions in Audit Event Ledger with Time Synchronization Service timestamps; end of tactical period decisions/issues to Analytics Warehouse for Post Operations Report. Flows: Flight Data Exchange normalizes FIM, sends filed flights to Demand Prediction Service, which compares with Airline Interface Adapter schedule (FIM primary on mismatch), uses

New part:
S108: The Weather Ingest Gateway accepts aviation forecasts, radar-derived precipitation fields, lightning alerts, wind forecasts, ceiling and visibility forecasts, and runway condition weather inputs from approved sources.
S109: Each weather feed is checked for source identity, issue time, valid time, spatial reference, and unit consistency before it is made available to the Regional Flow Platform.
S110: The Time Synchronization Service provides the reference clock used to compare forecast issue times with operational decision times.
S111: When a forecast product arrives late or fails validation, the Weather Ingest Gateway marks the feed as degraded rather than silently excluding it from the operational picture.
S112: The Meteorology Briefing Officer reviews degraded weather inputs when they affect capacity assumptions for the next planning period.
S113: Weather impacts are translated into capacity modifiers for runway configuration, arrival spacing, departure spacing, surface movement constraints, and approach sector availability.
S114: The North Runway Meter and South Runway Meter receive runway-specific capacity values after the Capacity Assessment Module applies the current wind, visibility, and precipitation assumptions.
S115: Surface constraints from the East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor are correlated with weather-driven taxi speed assumptions before the Ramp Movement Board is updated.
S116: The Airport Duty Manager may request a manual capacity review when local observations differ materially from the automated weather interpretation.
S117: The Regional Flow Manager uses the Common Situation Display to compare forecast demand, assessed capacity, and any active Ground Delay Program effects in one operational view.
S118: Forecast confidence is recorded as a confidence class, a probability value where provided by the source, a valid time range, and the forecast horizon used for the calculation.
S119: The confidence record also stores the originating feed, the processing time, the transformation version, and any manual override applied by the Meteorology Briefing Officer.
S120: Low-confidence weather forecasts remain visible to users, but the Capacity Assessment Module flags the associated capacity values as provisional.
S121: When confidence decreases below the configured threshold, the Alert Distribution Hub notifies the Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, and Airline Operations Coordinator that the capacity picture may change.
S122: All forecast confidence changes, feed quality changes, and capacity recalculations are written to the Collaborative Decision Log with synchronized timestamps.
S123: The Audit Event Ledger retains the trace from incoming forecast product to capacity value so that the Performance Analytics Warehouse can reconstruct the decision basis after operations.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
